correctness.rationale: For the all-path version of P3-convexity, a selected pair of neighbors forces any outside middle vertex into the set, whether or not the pair itself is adjacent. At a join, two selected vertices on one shore force the opposite shore to be selected in full; if both shore orders are at least two this forces the full graph. Apart from empty and singleton cases, the only other possible proper set selects one vertex per shore, and each must be isolated within its own shore to avoid an outside middle vertex. With a singleton factor u, omitting u permits only empty or singleton sets, while including u leaves no allowance for an edge from a selected to an outside vertex inside the other factor: the selected subset there must be a union of components. This proves both polynomial formulas (also K2, without double counting). A disjoint union splits the condition by factor; joins are connected with no isolates, so the auxiliary updates follow. A connected cograph with no universal vertex has a join decomposition with both orders at least two. Equality in i(A)i(B)≤|A||B|≤floor(n²/4) forces edgeless balanced shores and conversely gives the claimed graph. The O(n²) dense coefficient arithmetic bound follows by charging child-size products to pairs of leaves and array overhead to the sum of node sizes; the scalar updates are O(n) arithmetic using counts. Own replay: python3 /workspace/review_replay.py 4, scanning all graphs through order six with an induced-P4 detector, checking the actual predicted families against independent wedge implications; 6039 cographs, with 3, 10 and 10 labelled equality cases at orders 4, 5 and 6. This is a finite check; the supplied checker and saved output were inspected, not executed. Nonmaterial environment note: the supplied checker uses int.bit_count(), which needs Python ≥3.10 rather than the 3.9+ in its header.

Stars, P4, P5 and the subdivided-star extremizer are excluded from the sharp-bound class. The bipartite stability theorem is not over all connected cographs in that class.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The windmill specialization is actual coverage of that intersection, with no priority inferred from the same date. General cograph cones can have nonclique components, and joins of two factors of size at least two can yield non-block graphs such as K2,2. An invariant of extreme proper convex sets alone is not equivalent to counting every convex set by size.

originality.rationale: The star extremum, general algorithmic countability, and the overlapping windmill/complete-bipartite special cases are not credited as novel. The distinct finding is the explicit cardinality and structure of the convex sets at arbitrary cograph joins/unions and its sharp extremal consequence with unique balanced bipartite equality class in connected cographs without a universal vertex. No inspected statement implies that full package.

value.rationale: The formula answers an existing convex-set counting problem in a natural class while retaining cardinality information lost by scalar algorithms. It identifies a sharp quadratic alternative to the exponential star regime in connected cographs with no universal vertex, and characterizes exactly the extremal graphs. These contributions are more than an algorithmic application or a census.
